papers.title: Vacancy Engineering in Metals and Alloys
papers.abstract: Vacancy engineering, the intentional control of atomic-scale vacancies in metals and alloys, is emerging as a powerful yet underexplored strategy for tailoring microstructures and optimizing performance across diverse applications. By enabling excess vacancy populations through quenching, severe deformation, thermomechanical treatments, or additive manufacturing, new microstructures can be obtained that achieve unique combinations of strength, ductility, fatigue life, corrosion resistance, and conductivity. Vacancies are distinct among lattice defects: they are non-conserved entities essential for solute diffusion, yet variably coupled to solutes, dislocations, and phase boundaries. They can accelerate transformations such as nucleation and precipitation or retard kinetics when trapped in clusters, and their transient trapping and release can drive microstructural evolution across time and length scales. This Review synthesizes recent advances in generating, modeling, and characterizing vacancies, highlighting their role in diffusion, precipitation, and phase stability. Case studies in lightweight, high-temperature, fatigue-resistant, electrical, and biomedical materials demonstrate the broad potential of vacancy control. We conclude by emphasizing the opportunity for the metallurgical community to fully exploit excess vacancies as controllable, design-relevant defects that enable new pathways for microstructure and property optimization in next-generation alloys.

summary_en.motivation: The intentional control of atomic vacancies in metals and alloys is emerging as a powerful strategy to tailor microstructures and optimize mechanical and functional properties.
summary_en.method: This review synthesizes recent advances in generating, modeling, and characterizing vacancies, covering approaches such as quenching, severe deformation, thermomechanical treatments, and additive manufacturing.
summary_en.result: Vacancy engineering enables unique combinations of strength, ductility, fatigue life, corrosion resistance, and conductivity across various applications.
summary_en.validation: The paper is a review of existing literature and does not present new experimental validation.

papers.title: Frictional behavior between bone and additively manufactured Ti6Al4V implants is affected by bone density and surface texture under varying loads
papers.abstract: Friction at the bone-implant interface is a key factor in the initial stability of cementless orthopedic implants, largely affecting their long-term osseointegration behavior. Yet, there is limited data available for coefficients of friction (COFs) of different combinations of bone qualities and implant surface morphologies, particularly those produced by additive manufacturing techniques. This study measured the interfacial COFs of combinations of three levels of human cancellous bone qualities, characterized based on the BMD, and four Ti6Al4V micro and macro surface textures, produced using selective laser melting (SLM), under three levels of normal stress (0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 MPa), using a reciprocal friction test apparatus. Results indicated a wide range for the COF (0.37-0.95), significantly influenced by the individual effect of each of the metal surface roughness (strong positive: P-value < 0.05 and F-value = 19.12), bone density (moderate negative: P-value < 0.05 and F-value = 7.22) and normal stress (strong negative: P-value < 0.05 and F-value = 40.63), but not the interaction effects. A more variable frictional behavior was observed for both a lower density bone and a sharper-edged metallic texture, presumably due to the higher ploughing inconsistencies involved. The findings highlight the capability of SLM for developing COF-tailored patient-specific implants, based on personalized bone properties and biomechanical considerations.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not investigate any post-processing treatments or HIP; it focuses solely on as-printed SLM surface textures and their frictional behavior against bone.

summary_zh.motivation: 骨-植入物界面的摩擦是初始稳定性的关键因素，但不同骨质量和表面纹理的组合数据有限。
summary_zh.method: 采用往复摩擦测试装置，测量三种骨密度和四种SLM Ti6Al4V表面纹理在不同正应力下的摩擦系数。
summary_zh.result: 摩擦系数范围为0.37-0.95，受表面粗糙度、骨密度和正应力的显著影响，但无交互作用。
summary_zh.validation: 通过人松质骨与SLM Ti6Al4V试样的机械摩擦实验进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: Friction at the bone-implant interface is critical for initial stability, yet data on combinations of bone quality and additively manufactured surface textures are scarce.
summary_en.method: A reciprocal friction test apparatus was used to measure interfacial COFs for three levels of human cancellous bone density and four SLM Ti6Al4V surface textures under three normal stress levels.
summary_en.result: COFs ranged from 0.37 to 0.95, significantly influenced by surface roughness (strong positive), bone density (moderate negative), and normal stress (strong negative), with no significant interaction effects.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via mechanical friction experiments using human cancellous bone and SLM-fabricated Ti6Al4V specimens.

papers.title: An Analytical Framework for Correlation Between Laser Powder Bed Fusion Factors and Porosity-Induced Fracture Strength and Plasticity
papers.abstract: Strain-stress properties of additively manufactured materials by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) are substantially determined by the porosity level that is generated during the additive manufacturing. Accordingly, to optimally design of the LPBFed sample addressing the best stress-strain behavior, the porosity levels should be optimized through adjustment of process factors. In order to do so, in the present work, an integrated multi-physics-based analytical model has been developed to firstly correlate the LPBF process factors to porosity level using the mechanism of melt pool formation, vapor depression and identifying the lack-of-fusion. Then, the calculated porosity is used as an input of continuum damage mechanics model namely Gurson–Tvergaard–Needleman (GTN) to predict the stress-strain behavior. Through this hybrid approach, stress-strain curves together with ultimate tensile stress, elongation at peak and elongation at break have been successfully calculated and correlated to LPBF process factors. To verify the results, the LPBF samples made of stainless steel 316 L were subjected to micro-CT analysis and tensile testing and the measured values of porosity and stress-strain curves compared to the modded values. Also, comparisons were made on experimental values of porosity, UTS and elongation of other 3D printed materials i.e. Ti6Al4V, Inconel 718 and AlSi10Mg which reported in the literature with the values obtained from integrated framework in this research. The results based on relative root mean square error (RRMSE) showed that the developed model has excellent to good prediction accuracy with RRMSE values varies between the 3% to 20% accuracy in prediction of porosity, UTS and elongation of stainless steel 316 L, Ti6Al4V and Inconel 718. Also, for the aluminum alloy the RRMSE varies between 20% and 30% that shows the prediction accuracy is fair.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究LPBF工艺参数对力学性能的影响，但未涉及生物医学植入物或骨整合，与用户研究方向间接相关。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical implant context, no osseointegration, no fatigue testing; focus is on generic LPBF process-property relations for non-implant alloys.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过孔隙率预测LPBF零件的力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 集成熔池物理模型和GTN损伤模型预测应力应变行为。
summary_zh.result: 模型对316L等合金的UTS和延伸率预测误差在3%-30%。
summary_zh.validation: 微CT和拉伸试验验证，并与文献数据对比。

summary_en.motivation: To predict the fracture strength and plasticity of LPBF parts by correlating process parameters with porosity-induced damage.
summary_en.method: An integrated multi-physics analytical model combining melt pool formation and lack-of-fusion mechanisms with the GTN continuum damage model.
summary_en.result: The hybrid model predicted ultimate tensile stress and elongation with relative root mean square errors between 3% and 30% for 316L, Ti6Al4V, Inconel 718, and AlSi10Mg.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation using micro-CT porosity measurements and tensile tests on 316L samples, supplemented by literature data for other alloys.
